quote: 1) Existenz der Klassenkörper vom Relativgrade $2^{n}$ in Bezug auf $k(\sqrt{pq})$, indem man die Einheiten in diesem Körper und in den Körper $k(\sqrt{p}, \sqrt{q})$ studirt.
english: 1) Existence of class fields of relative degree 2^n with respect to k(√pq), by studying the units in this field and in the field k(√p, √q).
topic: A list of research and dissertation topics: the discriminant and invariants of the quartic, Poincaré cycles of differential equations, rotation of a body filled with fluid, three number-theoretic doctoral topics (class fields, Fermat's theorem, Weber's theorem), and independence of the laws 1-17 for complex number systems.

triage.modern_statement: Let K = Q(√(pq)) for distinct primes p, q. Its genus field K(√p, √q) = Q(√p, √q) is an unramified quadratic extension of K (in the narrow sense), so the 2-part of K's (narrow) class group is non-trivial. The task Hilbert set was to prove that K has unramified abelian 'class fields' of relative degree 2^n, for n beyond the genus level, matching the 2-power part of the class number. The suggested method was to compare the unit groups of K and of the biquadratic field Q(√p, √q). In modern terms this is a special case of the existence part of unramified (Hilbert) class field theory, applied to the 2-part of the class group of a real quadratic field with two ramified odd primes. It also asks for the finer structure of the 2-class group (its 4-rank and 8-rank), which governs whether unramified cyclic extensions of degree 4, 8, … exist.
triage.answered_by: The general existence of the Hilbert class field, which contains every such class field, was proved by Philipp Furtwängler in 1907. Takagi's existence theorem (around 1920) proved it for all abelian extensions. The explicit 2-power structure for quadratic fields like Q(√pq) was worked out by Rédei and Reichardt (4-rank, 1934) and Scholz (degree-8 fields, 1934). I could not find out which of Hilbert's doctoral students, if any, took this specific topic.

evidence.claim: Hilbert conjectured in 1898 that the (narrow) Hilbert class field exists and has certain properties, and proved this only when the class number is 2. Furtwängler proved existence in general in 1907.
The existence and uniqueness theorems of unramified class field theory can be proved following the original arguments of Hilbert and Furtwängler.
Takagi's existence theorem gives a correspondence between finite abelian extensions of a number field and generalized ideal class groups. This settles the existence of class fields in general.

In 1934 Rédei showed that the 4-rank of the class group of a quadratic field equals the nullity of a matrix over F_2 whose entries are Legendre symbols at the ramified primes. This determines when unramified degree-4 cyclic class fields exist over fields like Q(√pq).
Rédei began studying the 2-class group of quadratic fields Q(√d) in 1932, together with Reichardt and Scholz.
Research on the 4-rank of class groups of quadratic fields continues, e.g. Fouvry and Klüners, Inventiones 2007.

triage.why: This note is a dissertation topic: a special case of Hilbert's own 1898 conjecture that class fields exist. Furtwängler proved that conjecture in general in 1907, and Takagi extended it around 1920, so the existence question is settled. The detailed 2-power structure for Q(√pq) was clarified by Rédei, Reichardt and Scholz in 1934. It is not one of the 23 problems, though it is closely related to Problem 9 (reciprocity laws) and the class-field program. The distribution of 2-power ranks of class groups is still an active research area (Fouvry–Klüners, and recent arXiv work). Confidence is medium because I could not identify who carried out Hilbert's proposed method of comparing units, if anyone did. The sources link the solution to the general theorems, not to this exact diary entry.
